title: Your right to privacy of home and communication
summary: Your home, your correspondence, and your telephone conversations are private and protected. They cannot be intruded upon except by a procedure the law allows.
body_plain: The Constitution guarantees and protects the privacy of citizens, their homes, correspondence, telephone conversations and telegraphic communications. This is broader than your phone - it covers your house, your letters and messages, and your calls. Any search or interception must follow a procedure permitted by law, such as a valid warrant; it cannot simply be done because someone in authority wishes to.
rights: Your home, correspondence and communications are private (s.37).
A search of your home generally requires lawful authority such as a warrant.
Interception of your communications must follow a lawful procedure.
do_list: Ask to see a search warrant before anyone searches your home.
Watch and record what is searched or taken.
Note names, numbers and the time.
dont_list: Do not invite a search without asking about legal authority.
Do not sign a record of a search you have not read.
common_situations: Officers arrive at your home and ask to enter or search without explaining their authority.
A landlord, employer, or public official accesses private correspondence or communications.
People enter the home while you are absent and remove property or copy information.
words_to_use: I do not consent to entry or search. Please show me the authority you are relying on.
May I read the document and contact my lawyer before the search begins?
Please identify everyone entering and provide a record of anything removed.
if_violated: Prioritise safety; document names, vehicles, documents shown, rooms entered, and property removed afterward.
Preserve door-camera footage, photographs, witness details, messages, and proof of ownership.
Change compromised account credentials from a safe device and seek legal advice about privacy or property remedies.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
citations.quote: The privacy of citizens, their homes, correspondence, telephone conversations and telegraphic communications is hereby guaranteed and protected.
